concerns.message: The unit project in vitest.config.ts has no testTimeout, so each unit test gets vitest's default 5 s. Only the integration project raises it to 20 s. The new sweep is much larger than the one it replaces (360 lanes). It covers about 400 clear grid starts per dock across 9 docks (8 real plus the synthetic island), with 5 to 7 headings and 3 speeds each, for roughly 50–80k lanes of up to about 100 steps each. On this shared, contended machine that is plausibly 5–20 s.
concerns.consequence: Unless the `it` call passes an explicit timeout (for example 30_000) and the loop stops each lane early, `npm run test:unit` fails on a timeout even though every lane is correct. Or the sweep passes locally and times out under the verifier's load.

concerns.message: The plan doesn't say when a lane stops. Failures are raised only when a ship comes to rest inside the 5×5 block. A lane cut off by a short step cap, before it grounds or reaches an accepted step, is silently counted as 'sailed past'. A ship starting from rest 4 tiles out needs about 30+ world steps (acceleration 3, maxSpeed 39), and more if it slides along a coast.
concerns.consequence: A worker who shortens the cap to meet the 30 s budget can turn a real dead zone back into an uncounted pass-by: the same silent-skip problem this feature exists to remove.

concerns.message: The oracle is described per dock ('the berth tile or a neighbour'), but `sail` moors at whichever dock `dockInReach` returns among all docks. I checked the sketch: the shipped docks (17,21) and (23,27) are about 8.5 tiles apart, and no ring lane with a fixed heading reaches the other dock's neighbourhood. So this is latent, not live.
concerns.consequence: If a lane ever moors at a neighbouring dock, a per-dock oracle reports a confusing failure, or a mooring at the wrong dock goes unchecked. Writing the oracle over every dock and comparing the dock id costs nothing.

concerns.message: The quarter is mirrored, but the simulation is not mirror-exact: divTrunc truncates toward zero, and the flush-stop offsets (`column*size - 1 - half` against `(column+1)*size + half`) are asymmetric. So the rest tiles for the x- and y-mirrored copies of (17,21) and (23,27) may differ by a tile. I expect about 2 per dock, e.g. (21,28) and (25,27) at (23,27), and (17,19) and (17,23) at (17,21).
concerns.consequence: If the worker writes the exact list by mirroring one quarter's entries by hand, the exact-match assertion fails at some mirrored dock. The list has to come from the sweep's own output, with each entry's reason checked.

concerns.message: With 256-sub-unit tiles and a 384 reach, the reach disc lies inside the 3×3 neighbourhood. So the 'within reach with a clear run' fallback in both `dockInReach` and the test oracle never fires in the shipped game or on the synthetic island. Only the `dockRadius: 640` test exercises it.
concerns.consequence: The sweep proves nothing about the fallback clause, and a bug there would ship unseen. This is acceptable because decisions.md keeps the fallback, but the docs and review should not claim the sweep covers it.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: The plan as settled is already close to the simplest design, and I found no reason it can't work. Removing the spur is a one-row sketch edit that clears all four mirrored copies, and no validator depends on those tiles. The only real simplification would be to make `dockInReach` purely tile-based: the berth tile or its 8 neighbours, with the pinch guard and no reach fallback, because the fallback is dead code at 256/384. The behind-land negative test would then use a ship two tiles out behind land at the shipped reach. decisions.md keeps the fallback, though, so I would record this rather than reopen it.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Before the worker writes the final test, prototype the new `dockInReach` and the sweep loop. Stop each lane when it moors, comes to rest, or has moved past the 5×5 block in its heading's direction (with a fixed heading it can't come back), with a hard cap of 150 steps that is asserted never to be hit inside the block. Run it twice on the real map: once as is, once with sketch row 28's spur replaced by sea and the map regenerated. Print, per dock, the set of rest tiles and the wall-clock time. Expected: (22,29) and its mirrors appear only with the spur; about 2 rest tiles per dock and 2 on the synthetic island afterwards, differing slightly between mirrored docks; and a runtime that shows how large an explicit timeout the `it` call needs compared with the 5 s default.
